chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: 'Accursed! Accursed is the wealth from which Zakat is not paid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wealth from which Zakat has not been paid?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual purification aspect of Zakat by declaring accursed any wealth from which it is withheld. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that Zakat is not merely a legal obligation but a means of cleansing the soul and wealth from spiritual impurity. The repetition of 'ma'lun' (accursed) underscores the severity of neglecting this pillar of Islam.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Accursed! Accursed is the wealth not being purified (Zakāt not being paid from it)’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
condemned, and condemned indeed is (a property or) one who does not pay zakat.”
